newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends up on exports, funds buoy market.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends up on exports, funds buoy market.

text.p: Active exports, including confirmation by USDA that China continues to buy U.S. soymeal, boosted CBOT soymeal futures to a higher close, traders said.
Fund buying of soymeal and soyoil also was noted.

USDA said China bought 54,200 tonnes of U.S. soymeal during the week ended Nov 7. USDA said the net exports of U.S. soymeal that week totaled 221,500 tonnes, within the range of trade expectations for 150,000 to 300,000 tonnes.
Soyoil also was higher in step with the rally in soybeans and soymeal and the soyoil export tally in USDA's weekly report was generally constructive, the traders said.
USDA said the net exports of soyoil during the latest week were at 48,700 tonnes. The market was expecting from 60,000 to 80,000 tonnes.
Funds bought at least 3,700 lots of soymeal and bought at least 4,300 lots of soyoil.
Soymeal futures closed $1.40 to $3.00 per ton higher, with December up $3.00 at $234.30. Soyoil closed 0.30 to 0.40 cent per lb higher, with December up 0.37 at 23.53.
